theory.intro: Substituting a negative value is the same as any substitution, but you write the value in brackets. The brackets keep the negative sign attached when you multiply, subtract or take a power.
facts: **Always write a negative value in brackets** when you replace a pronumeral: $b = -2$ becomes $(-2)$.
Brackets stop a negative sign being misread as subtraction, and keep the sign attached through the order of operations.
**Multiplying signs:** like signs give a positive, unlike signs give a negative.
A negative to an **even** power is positive, $(-3)^2 = 9$, but to an **odd** power it stays negative, $(-2)^3 = -8$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate when $x=-8$. Show the substitution step.
(a) $x+5$
(b) $3x$
(c) $-2x$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $x+5=(-8)+5=-3$.
(b) $3x=3(-8)=-24$. Unlike signs give a negative product.
(c) $-2x=-2(-8)=16$. Like signs give a positive product.
Keep the negative value in brackets each time it replaces $x$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate $9-4b$ when $b=-3$.
A student writes $9-4(3)=-3$. Explain the error.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The student used $3$ instead of the given value $-3$.
$9-4b$
$=9-4(-3)$
$=9-(-12)$
$=9+12$
$=21$.
Substitute the whole negative value in brackets. Subtracting the negative product becomes adding.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate when $p=-2$. Explain why the answers differ.
(a) $3p^{2}$
(b) $(3p)^{2}$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) The square applies only to $p$.
$3p^{2}=3(-2)^{2}=3(4)=12$.
(b) The square applies to the whole bracket $3p$.
$(3p)^{2}=(3(-2))^{2}=(-6)^{2}=36$.
In (a), square the substituted value before multiplying by $3$. In (b), work out the whole bracket before squaring.

(a) Replace each pronumeral with its own negative value.
$2a-5b=2(-4)-5(-3)=-8-(-15)=-8+15=7$.
(b) Evaluate the powers first.
$a^{3}+b^{2}=(-4)^{3}+(-3)^{2}$
$=-64+9$
$=-55$.
Three negative factors give a negative cube. Two negative factors give a positive square.

workedExamples.question_text: Evaluate $\frac{3x+5}{4}$ when $x=-4$. Give an exact fraction.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Substitute the negative value in brackets. Work out the whole numerator before dividing.
$\frac{3x+5}{4}$
$=\frac{3(-4)+5}{4}$
$=\frac{-12+5}{4}$
$=\frac{-7}{4}$
$=-\frac{7}{4}$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate when $x=-5$.
(a) $x^{2}$
(b) $-x^{2}$
Explain what the minus sign in (b) applies to.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) $x^{2}=(-5)^{2}=(-5)(-5)=25$.
(b) $-x^{2}=-\left((-5)^{2}\right)=-25$.
The substituted value is bracketed in both expressions. In (b), the extra minus sign is outside the power, so take the negative of the completed square.
